solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notable meal continues with stimulating stuff

parts.note: something that continues lasts
an upper is a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: A memorable dinner goes on, fuelled by something to keep the diners lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ's final supper with the apostles is the most famous meal in Christian tradition, depicted by Leonardo.

clue.text: Money supporting a hair treatment

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so the money letter comes after the other piece

parts.note: a, as in 'five pounds a head', means per

explanation.surface: Someone pays for a salon session.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent wave is a salon process that sets curls into the hair chemically.

clue.text: College blocking legal right to observe grant-holder

indicators.note: the college letter sits in the way, stopping up the middle of the legal right

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
to observe is to see

explanation.surface: A college obstructs someone's legal entitlement to watch a scholarship recipient.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensee is someone granted a licence, such as a pub landlord, so is the holder of a grant of permission.

clue.text: Success capturing a Welsh knight

indicators.note: the word for success holds the other letters captive inside it

parts.note: a gain is a success or advance

explanation.surface: A Welsh knight wins by taking someone prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Welsh' looks like it describes the knight, but it supplies A and W.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain is one of the knights of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Tailless nag is acceptable for clockmaker

indicators.note: the tail of the word is cut off, removing its last letter

parts.note: to harry someone is to nag or pester them
something on is acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A horse with no tail is good enough for the man who builds clocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nag' looks like a horse but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: John Harrison was the eighteenth-century English inventor of the marine chronometer.

clue.text: Amateur engaged in homework, making audio device

indicators.note: the amateur letters are occupied within the homework word

parts.note: prep is British school slang for homework
AM is short for amateur

explanation.surface: A hobbyist busy with homework builds a piece of sound equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamplifier boosts a weak signal before it reaches the main amplifier in a sound system.

clue.text: Evaded crooks, accepting a bloke's credit in part of London

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take the other pieces inside them
to crook is to bend, so the letters of the first word are bent out of shape

parts.note: a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: Criminals dodged justice by taking a man's money in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooks' is a verb here, not criminals. 'Adam and Eve' is Cockney rhyming slang for 'believe', so to credit something in East London.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang, 'Adam and Eve' stands for believe, which is to credit.

clue.text: Attempt to include 'right' in sentence

indicators.note: the attempt word takes the right letter inside it

parts.note: a bid is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries to fit the word 'right' into a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a prison term, from rhyming slang 'birdlime' = time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing bird is British slang for serving time in prison, so a stretch inside.

clue.text: National material snapped in a camera

indicators.note: snapped means broken, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Pictures of a country's heritage are photographed on a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped' looks like photography, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts and material relating to the culture and history of the United States.

clue.text: Movable arms of sextants? Excellent couple

parts.note: rad is slang for excellent
II is the Roman numeral two, a couple

explanation.surface: Swinging sextant arms are great, and there are two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextant is a sixth of a circle, so its two straight sides are lines from the centre; the question mark admits the pun.

clue.text: Composure shown by artist's first painting technique

parts.note: to keep one's temper is to keep composure

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the artist word is used

explanation.surface: An artist's early work shows calm in its method.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg yolk, used widely before oils.

clue.text: Set up marine area with new weapons

parts.note: to rear is to raise or set up
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A naval zone is established and equipped with fresh arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been armed again, a force is supplied with fresh weaponry.

clue.text: Rebellions forcing US to intervene? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece is to come between the letters of the other
reverses the instruction, so the forcing word goes inside the US letters rather than US inside it

parts.note: prising is forcing open

explanation.surface: Revolts that push America into stepping in, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisings are revolts against authority.

clue.text: Party person regarding supplier of drinks

parts.note: re means regarding or about
a publican runs a pub

explanation.surface: A partygoer is talking about the man who serves the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party person' suggests a reveller, but it means a member of a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Republican Party is a party member in the political sense.

clue.text: Secretary, mostly fastidious, exhibiting alarm

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: nice can mean fastidious or precise

explanation.surface: A fussy secretary shows signs of fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic and alarm are both sudden fear.

clue.text: Make up for security group getting involved in fight?

indicators.note: the security group letters end up inside the fight word

parts.note: to compete is to fight or contend
the NSA is the US National Security Agency

explanation.surface: A security outfit joins a scrap, perhaps to settle a score.
explanation.definitionFit: To compensate is to make amends or offset a loss.

clue.text: Sweet salad plant, untouched — the best

parts.note: a pepper is a vegetable eaten in salads
in mint condition means untouched
the cream is the best part

explanation.surface: A salad vegetable, pristine, is top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppermint cream is a mint-flavoured fondant confection.

clue.text: Bush bud topped — happy about that?

indicators.note: the happy word goes round the other piece

parts.note: merry means happy

indicators.note: the top letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a bulb is a bud-like underground shoot

explanation.surface: A shrub's bud has been cut back; is the gardener pleased?
explanation.definitionFit: The mulberry is a tree or bush, as in the nursery rhyme 'Here we go round the mulberry bush'.

clue.text: Caught you finally when probing less adequate spinner?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the letter pushes its way into the middle of the other word

parts.note: ropy means of poor quality, so ropier is less adequate

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A cricketer is caught out probing a weaker spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a cricket spin bowler; it is the roulette dealer who spins the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs a casino table, spinning the roulette wheel.

clue.text: Nonconformist recalled unpleasant look about book

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the book letter
called back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a leer is a nasty look

explanation.surface: A dissenter remembered someone glaring over a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns LEER into REEL, which then goes round B.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel refuses to conform to authority or convention.

clue.text: Some will support literary catalogue

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes last

parts.note: lit is short for literary, as in lit crit
any can mean some, as in 'is there any milk?'

explanation.surface: A portion of something will back a bookish list.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long recital or list, like a catalogue of complaints.

clue.text: Finished year occupying isolated tourist attraction

indicators.note: the other pieces settle inside the isolated word

parts.note: lone means isolated
done means finished

explanation.surface: A completed year spent at a remote visitor site.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Eye is the giant observation wheel on the South Bank of the Thames.

clue.text: Note one upset about company exhibiting traditional values

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the company letters
upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A memo upsets someone at a firm with old-fashioned principles.
explanation.definitionFit: A neoconservative holds conservative, traditional political views.

clue.text: Game allowed to finish early — with this sound?

parts.note: whist is a card game

indicators.note: the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A match is permitted to end ahead of time with the referee's signal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures the referee's final call, which is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle is a shrill sound, the kind a referee makes to stop play.

clue.text: Mostly discreet over husband's desire

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over the second
most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: wise can mean prudent or discreet
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A tactful partner is mostly what a husband wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish is a desire or longing.

clue.text: New opus here curtailed for classical musician

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are put together in a different order
the tail of the word is cut, dropping its last letter

explanation.surface: A fresh composition here is cut short for a classical performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus was the legendary musician of Greek myth whose lyre charmed even the underworld.

clue.text: Calm incident, not tense

indicators.note: the word is taken without the tense letter

parts.note: an event is an incident
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A peaceful happening without any tension.
explanation.definitionFit: Even can mean calm and steady, as in an even temper.

clue.text: Mark left, abandoning despot

indicators.note: the left letter quits the despot's name

parts.note: Stalin was the Soviet dictator

explanation.surface: A mark remains after a tyrant is deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a discoloured mark or blemish.

clue.text: Catastrophic vote loser: US President

indicators.note: a catastrophe throws things into disorder, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A disastrous election loser becomes an American president.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Theodore Roosevelt were both presidents of the United States.
